core_obligations: Consider the ring A' = A[x]/(x^n - pi) with pi' the image of x in A_1, and note that A' is finite free of rank n over A (proof lines 33970-33971).
Deduce that pi is a nonzerodivisor in A' and hence so is pi', and that A'/pi'A' is isomorphic to the field A/pi A, so A' is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer pi' (proof lines 33972-33974).
Conclude that the fraction field K' of A' is an extension of K of degree n and is obtained by adjoining an n-th root of pi, so K' is isomorphic to K_1 (proof lines 33975-33977).
Use that A' is normal to conclude that A' is the integral closure A_1 of A in K_1, which proves parts (1) to (5) (proof lines 33978-33979).
Observe that K_1/K is tamely ramified when n is invertible in the residue field, immediately from the definition together with parts (3) and (4) (proof lines 33982-33984).
For the last statement, reduce by Kummer theory to showing that every n-th root of unity zeta in K' lies in K (proof lines 33985-33987).

Write zeta = a + b with a in A and b in the direct sum of A(pi')^j for 1 <= j <= n-1; if b is nonzero, write b = u(pi')^t with t >= 1 and u a unit, and use 1 = zeta^n = a^n + n a^{n-1} u (pi')^t modulo (pi')^{t+1} to force b congruent to (1 - a^n)/(n a^{n-1}) modulo (pi')^{t+1}, which contradicts the direct sum decomposition because the image of multiplication by (pi')^{t+1} meets A(pi')^t in (pi A)(pi')^t; hence b = 0 and zeta lies in A (proof lines 33988-34002).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A with uniformizer pi and an integer n >= 2, sets K_1 = K[pi^{1/n}], and asserts six things: that the degree is n, that the integral closure A_1 is the ring A[pi^{1/n}], that A_1 is a discrete valuation ring, that the ramification index over A is n, that K_1 is totally ramified with respect to A, and that when n is prime to the residue characteristic K_1/K is tamely ramified with every subextension generated by pi^{1/d} for a divisor d of n (source lines 33953-33967). The first five parts are established through the auxiliary ring A' = A[x]/(x^n - pi): the proof observes that A' is finite free of rank n over A, so pi is a nonzerodivisor in A' and hence so is the image pi' of x; since A'/pi'A' is isomorphic to the field A/pi A, the ring A' is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer pi', its fraction field K' has degree n over K and is obtained by adjoining pi^{1/n}, and because A' is normal it is the integral closure A_1 (proof lines 33970-33979). The tameness assertion is then immediate from the definition and parts (3) and (4) (proof lines 33982-33984). The final statement about subextensions is the substantive part: it suffices to show every n-th root of unity zeta in K' lies in K, for which the proof notes zeta is a unit of A', writes zeta = a + b with a in A and b in the direct sum of the A(pi')^j for 1 <= j <= n-1, and argues by contradiction. If b were nonzero, writing b = u (pi')^t with t >= 1 and u a unit, the congruence 1 = zeta^n = a^n + n a^{n-1} u (pi')^t modulo (pi')^{t+1} would force b to be congruent to (1 - a^n)/(n a^{n-1}) in A modulo (pi')^{t+1}, which the direct sum decomposition A' = A oplus ... oplus A(pi')^{n-1} rules out because the image of multiplication by (pi')^{t+1} meets A(pi')^t in (pi A)(pi')^t (proof lines 33985-34002). The non-routine content is this congruence argument against the direct sum decomposition.
